deck.topic: Texas market reality check: price cuts vs concessions

points.title: Inventory Is Back
body: Texas has more homes for sale than it has had in over a decade.
Buyers have real choices again, so nobody feels rushed.
points.loop: The clock is doing something too.

points.title: Homes Sit Longer Now
body: The first two weeks is when a listing gets its real attention.
After that the showings thin out and the calls slow down.

points.title: The Price Cut Trap
body: Four out of ten sellers respond by dropping the number.
Buyers read a price cut as blood in the water and wait for the next one.
points.loop: The rest moved a lot quieter.

points.title: What The Other Six Did
body: They left the list price alone and paid the buyer instead.
Closing costs covered. Rate bought down. Repairs handled up front.
The seller nets more and the buyer feels it every single month.
points.loop: Buyers leave this on the table.

points.title: Ask For The Money
body: Right now you can ask a seller to cover costs and still win the house.
Put it in the offer. Not after the inspection, when your leverage is already spent.
points.loop: Your street is not the average.

linkedinCaption:
Texas has more homes on the market than it has in over a decade. That changes how a listing behaves after week two, when showings thin out and the phone gets quiet.

About four in ten sellers react by cutting the price. Buyers tend to read that as a signal to wait for the next one.

The other six hold the list price and pay the buyer directly. Closing costs. A rate buydown. Repairs handled before the inspection. The seller often nets more, and the buyer feels the benefit every month.

For buyers, the ask belongs in the original offer, not after inspection when leverage is gone.

Are you seeing concessions hold value better than price reductions in your market?
